title: Review
description: Output of Phase 2 (architectural tier only; the standard tier replaces the reviewer fan-out with constraints.md injection). DBA, DevOps, and SecOps each write their block via per-agent shards the orchestrator merges.

secops.description: A SecOps finding can occupy three locations, and the property requirement reaches only two of them. concerns[] requires must_satisfy and vulnerabilities[] requires remediation, both refused at SubagentStop. compliance_flags[] is UNREACHED: its items subschema has no required list at all, so a VETO recorded as {verdict: VETO, concerns: [], vulnerabilities: [], compliance_flags: [{}]} validates SILENT, with no statute, no concern and no action - measured through the shipped hook, with the pre-change schemas as the non-zero control. That channel is named here rather than guarded: guarding it needs its own cost analysis against already-written compliance rows and is not this change's business. The set is quantified over LOCATIONS a blocking finding can occupy, taken from the artifact contract in agents/secops.md, so a fourth location added later is visibly missing rather than silently absent.

statute.description: # CUSTOMIZE: the regulation or policy this concern maps to for your domain (e.g. GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, an internal data-handling policy). Free-form so it fits any jurisdiction.

remediation.description: This field KEEPS its name and changes its contract: what a correct fix must SATISFY, stated as a property carrying the observation that decides it ('the endpoint must be rate-limited low enough that credential stuffing and bulk scraping are not economical, measured by <observation: N requests from one source inside M seconds are rejected before the handler runs>'), or, where an authority outside you fixed the value, that value stated literally with a source a reader can OPEN AND FIND THAT LITERAL IN - a self-identifying standard NAME is its own locator and needs no citation clause ('the webhook signature must be verified with the provider's HMAC-SHA256 scheme'). NAMING A DOCUMENT THAT DOES NOT ITSELF FIX THE LITERAL IS WORSE THAN NAMING NONE, because an invented bound then acquires a citation's authority: 'at most 3 attempts, per OWASP ASVS' is OUT unless that standard fixes 3 and you can say where, and 'at most 6 attempts, per the applicable card-data standard's authentication requirements' is OUT one step earlier, because it DESCRIBES a source instead of NAMING one and so leaves a reader nothing to open at all - a form-level call needing no standard in hand - while 'the TOTP time step must be the 30 seconds RFC 6238 section 5.2 fixes as its default' is IN, naming the document AND the place inside it. Those three worked cases are the check on this sentence: they and the 'Two things stay allowed' clause replicated in the ten files that carry it (nine agent contracts and the slash-command template) are one rule stated twice, and a statement of it that admits either OUT case, or refuses the IN one, is the defective one. BEFORE YOU PROPAGATE THEM, RE-APPLY THE UMBRELLA TO THE IN CASE ITSELF: hand a reader only the quoted ask and require them to reach the place that fixes the literal; if no document is nameable from that string alone, that case belongs in the OUT column and this sentence needs a NEW in case rather than a reworded old one. Edit either copy and re-apply all three to both. Not a mechanism: 'wrap it with the global rate-limit middleware' names one implementation, forecloses the others, and cannot be checked without reading that middleware. A mechanism you weighed goes in rationale_not_checked. THE EMPTY STRING SATISFIES this field: the walker implements no minLength, and 17 of 229 already-written vulnerability rows carry no remediation at all (info 9, low 4, medium 4; ZERO of the 3 critical and ZERO of the 26 high), so '' is what a no-remediation row will become rather than a refusal. What you write here is copied into knowledge/issue-archive/<n>.json, which IS committed, and 'verbatim' is not quite true of that copy: it runs through the absolute-path redactor in knowledge-store.mjs, so a remediation that OPENS with a route loses that route ('/v1/public-feed must be unreachable without a server-validated bearer token' archives with its subject replaced). The invariant true under both redactor forms is that a LEADING path span does not survive, so put the route mid-sentence or the archived property loses its subject; everything else is copied as written. Because that copy is public and nothing but a leading path span is rewritten, never paste credential material into this field - and read that as a rule you honor, not a control that protects you: there is no length check, no pattern check and no redaction of credential material on this path, so a pasted secret validates clean and is archived as written.

rationale_not_checked.description: OPTIONAL, and never in any required list. The non-binding landing spot for a candidate mechanism you weighed in order to test a property's COST or falsify its necessity. No downstream role owes this field an action.

severity.description: This schema is the single source of truth for concern severity. The canonical panel vocabulary is blocker|major|nit (DBA/DevOps/Design emit these); SecOps's CVE-style critical|high|medium|low|info is accepted alongside it so a SecOps concern (e.g. severity 'low') validates cleanly. Distinct from the knowledge_drift_claims severity field.

must_satisfy.description: What a correct fix must BE TRUE OF, carrying in itself the observation whose outcome decides whether it is met - never HOW to make it true. A mechanism you weighed goes in rationale_not_checked. TWO ROLES ARE EXEMPT, recorded here because the rule is unreadable without it: QA and Dev own solution design through the TDD contract, so a QA or Dev concern that specifies a test, a matrix or a mechanism is IN BOUNDS, and this field is where it goes. (a) WHERE A MISSING PROPERTY IS REFUSED, stated over the PAIR that decides it - the STOPPING AGENT'S TYPE and the artifact - because a location alone decides nothing: three agent types are refused, dba, devops and secops, on this field in Phase 2 concerns[] and on remediation in SecOps vulnerabilities[]. THE ARTIFACT SET IS TWO FILES PER TYPE, NOT ONE: reviewerRules gives each of those three both its own review.<role>.json shard AND the MERGED review.json at /<role> (validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:86-89 lists the four rules; :88 is the merged one), so the refusal is keyed to the STOP and not to the moment of writing. A merged Phase 2 record is re-read at every later stop of the same type while its mtime is inside the 30-minute window, which is how a Phase 4 reviewer gets blocked on a Phase 2 block it did not write. MEASURED ON THIS CHANGE'S OWN RUN, roots = repo root, active issue 40: checkArtifacts returns 4 failures for dba, 2 for devops and 5 for secops, every one of them 'review.json/<role> /concerns[N]: missing required field "must_satisfy"' on rows written in Phase 2 before this contract existed; ba, dev, librarian, design and art-director return none at all in the same run, and qa returns none on review.json - its 4 are on peer-review.json, for a severity value outside that enum, which is a different defect in a different file. That partition is the non-zero control: the fixture is not simply blocking everything. WHAT TO DO WHEN IT HAPPENS: let the file age past the 30-minute window, or re-run the Phase 2 reviewer that owns the block. Do NOT backfill a property into another role's finished record, and least of all '', which writes a property nobody stated into a record that is about to be archived. README 'Upgrading' item 14 says the same thing to an operator deciding whether to upgrade mid-run. NO OTHER AGENT TYPE IS REFUSED ON ANY PHASE 2 ARTIFACT: design and art-director have no AGENT_RULES entry at all, and ba, dev, qa and librarian have entries that reach no review shard, so Design - a real Phase 2 reviewer - writes an unvalidated one. Measure that rather than trusting it: run one shard whose concerns[0] omits this field through hooks/subagent-stop.sh once per agent type, against a shard the current schema already refuses as the non-zero control. NOT on SecOps compliance_flags[], whose items subschema has no required list at all - a VETO recorded as {verdict: VETO, concerns: [], vulnerabilities: [], compliance_flags: [{}]} validates SILENT, with no statute, no concern and no action, measured through the shipped hook. NOT on any Phase 4 peer-review artifact (#38). (b) THE ENFORCEMENT RECORD IS DATED AND SCOPED BY DEPLOYMENT MODE, never by repository identity. WINDOW: measured 2026-08-21. POPULATION, with its inclusion rule stated because the corpus is larger than the count: one machine's ~/.claude/projects, walked RECURSIVELY - subagent transcripts live in per-session SUBDIRECTORIES, and a top-level-only walk sees 82 of 1680 files and finds ZERO blocks, which is output-identical to the finding it is supposed to test. 13 repositories in that corpus hold any transcript; the 8 counted here are those carrying pipeline activity of either kind, at least one block or at least one namespaced dispatch, and they held 1638 files / 353,907 lines when this was written. THE CORPUS IS LIVE AND ONLY GROWS: re-run hours later it reads 1680 files / 366,314 lines over all 13, and 1662 / 362,734 over the 8. What must reproduce is the partition, not the absolute. FINDING: 56 genuine blocks, every one of them in a project that dispatches BARE agent names from local .claude/agents/*.md files; ZERO across 670 plugin-namespaced dispatches in SEVEN repositories - 645 of them excluding the 25 this change's own session had recorded when the figure was taken - one of which is an adopting project directory with 362. ONE COUNTING RULE FOR BOTH FIGURES, pipeline agents only, and MIND THE GRAIN: at the recipe's project-directory grain that adopting directory shows 362 and its other-plugin set is EMPTY. The 365 belongs to the REPOSITORY grain, which sums that directory with a second project directory for the same repository where 3 dispatches of another plugin's agent live; that plugin's agent is one this hook could not have refused under any repair. Two grains, two numbers, and the recipe below states only the first. RE-DERIVATION, and run it rather than reading it: walk every *.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects RECURSIVELY (the subagent transcripts are in subdirectories), count messages whose message.content is a plain string beginning 'Stop hook feedback:\nPipeline artifact failed schema validation', group by project directory; then cross-tabulate against the subagent_type field of the recorded subagent-dispatch tool_use entries, selecting those entries by tool name IN ('Task','Agent'). BOTH NAMES, and this is the step that decides whether the paragraph re-derives at all: on the corpus above the host recorded 'Agent' 1623 times, rising with every session run since, and 'Task' ZERO times, so a cross-tabulation keyed on 'Task' alone comes back EMPTY in every repository - output-identical to the zero-blocks finding it is supposed to test. ITS NON-ZERO CONTROL: the dispatch count must come back non-zero before any zero-block figure means anything; if it does not, your selector missed the tool rather than the corpus missing the dispatches. Then run the four-cell agent_type fixture ('secops', 'SecOps', 'pipeline:secops', 'agent-pipeline:secops') against the shipped hook. The installed plugin with namespaced names is the shipping default, so read this as a dated record and not as a warranty for your deployment. AND EVERY ENFORCEMENT CLAIM HERE DESCRIBES THE SOURCE TREE at that date: an installed plugin runs its own cached copy of these schemas and of the agent contracts until that installation is refreshed, so a claim true on the integration branch is not yet true in a session running the cache. Filed as #66; the correct outcome for #66 is that somebody fixes it, on which day this paragraph becomes false and a silence has no event that notices. (c) THE FAIL-OPEN DEGRADATIONS, five of them: the enforced half degrades to nothing when node is absent, when the plugin root is unset, when the active issue is unresolvable, when the artifact's mtime exceeds 30 minutes, and - dominantly, and this is the one that screens off the other four - when the stopping agent's type does not match an AGENT_RULES key (validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:93 for the keys, :654-656 for the lookup and its early return). (d) THE EMPTY STRING SATISFIES. The walker implements no minLength and the requirement cannot be conditioned on severity, so '' is the cheapest value that satisfies this field. Measured 2026-08-21 over the bare-name deployments where the gate fires, and that population is stated as a RULE YOU CAN RUN rather than as a list of checkouts, because 'the deployments where it fires' is not walkable while a list of names would scope this record by IDENTITY, which (b) forbids for exactly the reason it would be wrong here too - identity is an accident of one machine, the deployment mode is the property. THE RULE: enumerate every checkout under the projects root and keep the ones whose .claude/agents/ directory holds THIS pipeline's own agent files by name (ba, dba, devops, secops, dev, qa, librarian, design, art-director). On the machine this was measured on, exactly TWO checkouts qualify; three further checkouts carry local agents that are NOT this pipeline's and dispatch namespaced, and the same rule excludes them without a judgement call. That is a DIFFERENT and much larger population than the knowledge/issue-archive/ folder beside this schema: 17 of 229 already-written vulnerability rows there carry no remediation - info 9, low 4, medium 4, and ZERO of the 3 critical and ZERO of the 26 high. Counting the local archive will not reproduce that denominator and is not meant to. HOW THE 229 WAS REACHED, because a reader who gets a different number will blame the record rather than the glob, and each near miss below is one a reader actually hit: EVERY .pipeline directory in those two checkouts was walked, including the ones under .claude/worktrees, and vulnerabilities[] was counted in BOTH artifact families. The top-level .pipeline directories alone give 101 rows and 16 without remediation; the review family alone gives 210 and 16, because 19 of the 229 rows sit in peer-review files and 1 of the 17 with them. Concerns rows count only entries that are OBJECTS - 9 non-object entries, all in the peer family, are excluded, and one file in the corpus does not parse at all. AND UNLIKE THE CORPUS IN (b), THIS ONE CAN SHRINK: it is counted over working checkouts whose .claude/worktrees get PRUNED, so growth is not the only direction and a later walk can land BELOW every denominator here. Read a smaller number as the population moving; read a changed PARTITION as the record drifting. THAT 17-OF-229 IS ONE HALF OF THIS MIGRATION; THE OTHER HALF IS 100%, and a reader who takes 7% away as the retroactive scale has the wrong number. Same population, same walk, same day: 996 already-written concerns rows, not one of them carrying must_satisfy. Against the merge-base required list [severity, description], 185 of 996 fail; against the shipped list [severity, description, must_satisfy], 996 of 996 fail. MIND THE GRAIN ON BOTH, because those 996 span two artifact families with different contracts. 488 sit in review.json and review.<role>.json, which agentBlock's required list governs: 0 of those 488 failed the merge-base list and 488 of 488 fail the shipped one, so on the population this change actually governs the already-written failing fraction moves from 0% to 100%. The other 508 sit in peer-review.json and peer-review.<role>.json, whose items subschema has no required list at all (#38) - every one of the 185 merge-base failures is in that half, and none of them is refused by anything. None of those rows is revalidated once its file passes the 30-minute window; what IS revalidated is a merged review.json in a run still in flight, which clause (a) measures and states. The empty-string residual itself is tracked in #71, which also carries the wider class of free-text reviewer fields that cross the same archived-and-committed boundary with no note of any kind on them. (e) THE ARCHIVE RESIDUAL. What you write here is copied verbatim into knowledge/issue-archive/<n>.json, which IS committed, and that copy runs through the absolute-path redactor in knowledge-store.mjs. A property that OPENS with a route is rewritten: origin/main today carries LEADING_SPAN (knowledge-store.mjs:147), which replaces the leading path span only and leaves the prose after it standing; the earlier ABSOLUTE_VALUE form replaced the WHOLE value, prose and all. The invariant true under BOTH forms, and the only one to rely on, is that a LEADING path span does not survive into the durable record - so put the route mid-sentence or the archived property loses its subject. Check which form is live rather than trusting this sentence: grep -n 'ABSOLUTE_VALUE\|LEADING_SPAN' plugins/pipeline/scripts/knowledge-store.mjs. Because that copy is verbatim and public, never paste credential material into this field - and read that as a rule you honor, not a control that protects you: there is no length check, no pattern check and no redaction of credential material on this path, so a pasted secret validates clean and is archived as written. (f) THE NEIGHBOUR LIMIT. This annotation warrants nothing beyond its own field: nothing about compliance_flags[], which stays unguarded by design; nothing about the severity enum above it; and nothing about agentBlock's BLOCK-LEVEL required list [verdict, reviewed_at, concerns, notes], which this change does not touch. Read that last clause exactly: the ITEM-level required list on this very subschema IS edited by this change - it becomes [severity, description, must_satisfy] - and the two lists are different objects at different depths. (g) THIS SUBSCHEMA IS DELIBERATELY OPEN, and no check in this repository enforces that. Neither it nor the other two subschemas this change edited (SecOps vulnerabilities[].items in review.schema.json, panelVerdict concerns[].items in peer-review.schema.json) declares additionalProperties, and that openness is what makes the added required field REVERSIBLE: an instance written under the new contract, carrying keys the old one never declared, still validates against the pre-change schemas. Closing any of the three turns a reversible addition into a one-way migration on the day these artifacts meet a conformant validator. DO NOT READ THAT AS A GUARDED INVARIANT: the shipped walker implements no additionalProperties keyword at all - it handles type, enum, required, properties, minItems, items and allOf - so planting additionalProperties:false on any of the three reddens nothing: not the self-test, not the hook, not the suite. It is a written invariant with no enforcement, recorded here because here is where the next editor of this subschema is looking.

rationale_not_checked.description: OPTIONAL, and never in any required list, in any of the three subschemas that carry it. The non-binding landing spot for a candidate mechanism you weighed in order to test a property's COST or falsify its necessity - which the guardrail rule asks you to do. No downstream role owes this field an action, and a fix that ignores it is not thereby wrong. Keeping it separate is what lets must_satisfy stay a property.

notes.description: Free-text reasoning. String preferred; an array of strings is accepted (agents emit both in practice).
